requirements.text: Each lamp forming part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear position lamp P-01, stop lamp P-02, reversing lamp P-03, and the integral rear retro-reflector P-05) shall satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of another UN Regulation. [UN R148 para. 3.2.2]
Any lamp that does not satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of another UN Regulation shall not be part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp unit. [UN R148 para. 3.2.2]

Each light signalling function of the lamp shall be identified by the symbol specified in UN R148 para. 3.2.4, Table 1: rear position lamp R1 (steady) or R2 (variable); stop lamp S1 (steady) or S2 (variable); reversing lamp AR (the letters A and R may be mingled). [UN R148 para. 3.2.4, Table 1]

Every device belonging to the approved lamp type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in UN R148 paras. 3.3.3.2 to 3.3.3.6. [UN R148 para. 3.3.1.1]
All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible. [UN R148 para. 3.3.1.1.1]
The dimension 'a' of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm. [UN R148 para. 3.3.1.2]

The approval marking shall include the approval mark, consisting of a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.1]
The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number prescribed in UN R148 para. 3.2.3.2. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.2]
The four- to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.2]

The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying each light signalling lamp function prescribed in UN R148 para. 3.2.4 (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp). [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.3]

The approval marking shall include the number of the Regulation followed by the letter 'R' (i.e. '148R') and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time the approval is issued. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.4]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately): The lamp shall bear, as part of the approval marking, a horizontal arrow showing the position in which the lamp is to be mounted. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.1]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp bears the horizontal mounting arrow per para. 3.3.2.5.1): For the rear position lamp function, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.1.1 (b); parent R148-base-0012]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the reversing lamp has reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps and the lamp bears the horizontal mounting arrow): For the reversing lamp function, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.1.1 (c); parent R148-base-0012]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps): The lamp shall bear the additional letter 'D' to the right of the function symbol specified in UN R148 para. 3.2.4. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.2]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system): The lamp shall bear the additional letter 'Y' to the right of the function symbol specified in UN R148 para. 3.2.4. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.2]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the lamp has reduced light distribution as defined in UN R148 Annex 3 para. 1.1): The lamp shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards. [UN R148 para. 3.3.2.5.3]
The lamp shall bear the approval marking. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.1]
The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.2]
Because the lamp uses non-replaceable light sources, it shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or of the range of voltage. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.4]

CONDITIONAL (applies if an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body): That control gear or variable luminous intensity control shall be marked with its identification number. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.6]

CONDITIONAL (applies if an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body): That control gear or variable luminous intensity control shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer. [UN R148 para. 3.3.3.6]

The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part of the lamp (outer lens P-04). [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.1]

The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle, or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened. Any prescribed LED substitute light source category shall be visible under the same conditions. [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.2]

The approval marking and the markings of UN R148 paras. 3.3.3.2 (trade name or mark), 3.3.3.3, 3.3.3.4 (rated voltage), 3.3.3.5 (b) and 3.3.3.6 (where applicable) shall be affixed on the lamp. [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.5]

The markings of UN R148 paras. 3.3.3.2 (trade name or mark), 3.3.3.3 (a), 3.3.3.4 (rated voltage), 3.3.3.5 and 3.3.3.6 shall not be required to fulfil the visibility-when-fitted requirement of para. 3.3.4.2. The approval marking remains subject to para. 3.3.4.2. [UN R148 para. 3.3.4.7; relaxation related to R148-base-0035]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the single approval mark option is selected): Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations (e.g. R148 for the lamp functions and R150 for the retro-reflector), the lamp shall bear a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number. [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.1; permissive option]

CONDITIONAL (applies if a single approval mark is used per para. 3.3.5.1): The single approval mark of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be located where it is visible after installation of the lamps. [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.1.1; parent R148-base-0041]

CONDITIONAL (applies if a single approval mark is used per para. 3.3.5.1): The single approval mark of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be located such that no light-transmitting part of the lamps can be removed without also removing the approval mark. [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.1.2; parent R148-base-0041]

CONDITIONAL (applies if a single approval mark is used on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps): The size of each component of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval has been granted (e.g. R148 and R150). [UN R148 para. 3.3.5.2; parent R148-base-0041]

Each lamp function submitted for approval under UN R148 (rear position lamp P-01, stop lamp P-02, reversing lamp P-03) shall conform to the requirements in paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.1]

The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN R48 (and the Annexes referenced there), in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp. The requirements pertinent to each lamp function and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible. [UN R148 para 4.2]

The lamp (including housing P-08, fasteners P-10, optical parts and LED PCB) shall be designed and constructed so that, in normal conditions of use and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.3]

CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D'): the 'D' approval shall be used only for the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp functions (including rear end-outline marker lamp). It shall not be applied to the reversing lamp function, which is not among the functions listed. [UN R148 para 4.4.1]

CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is approved as part of an interdependent lamp system marked 'Y'): the 'Y' approval shall be used only for the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp functions (including rear end-outline marker lamp). It shall not be applied to the reversing lamp function, which is not among the functions listed. [UN R148 para 4.4.2]
The rear position lamp function (P-01), when approved as a rear position lamp under UN R148, shall be regarded as also approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp. [UN R148 para 4.5.1]

The rear position lamp function (P-01), being grouped (or combined/reciprocally incorporated) with the stop lamp and reversing lamp, may also be used as a rear end-outline marker lamp. [UN R148 para 4.5.2]

CONDITIONAL (if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source and is designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted): this arrangement is permitted under UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.5.3]

CONDITIONAL (if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp using a common light source): these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (e.g. a double filament light source), or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps. [UN R148 para 4.5.3.1]

CONDITIONAL (on request of the applicant, if a manufacturer logo is incorporated): the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of the lamp function may incorporate only one manufacturer logo, built by transparent or non-transparent components. This is permitted provided that all requirements of UN R148 for the specific function are fulfilled and the conditions of paragraph 4.5.5 (a) to (d) are met. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]

CONDITIONAL (if a logo is incorporated): irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be incorporated in the apparent surface of the lamp. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]

CONDITIONAL (if a logo is incorporated): the enclosed light emitting surface of the incorporated logo (including transparent and non-transparent components of the logo), in the direction of the reference axis, shall not exceed 100 cm2. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]

CONDITIONAL (if a logo is incorporated): notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2 of UN R48, the logo light emitting surface (including transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) is not required to be symmetrical by itself. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]
The stop lamp function (P-02) and the reversing lamp function (P-03) shall not incorporate a logo. [UN R148 para 4.5.5]

In each single lamp function containing more than one LED light source, any group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source for the purposes of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.6.1.1]

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp function containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3 of UN R148, and the maximum intensities are not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure is produced, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8, 6.7.8, 6.9.8, 6.10.8, 6.11.8, 6.12.8, 6.13.8 and 6.18.8 of UN R48, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure. [UN R148 para 4.6.1.2]

CONDITIONAL (if rear position lamp R2 and/or stop lamp S2 is chosen): in case of failure of the variable intensity control of an R2 (or RM2) or S2 lamp emitting more than the maximum value of category R1 (RM1) or S1 respectively, the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1 (RM1) or S1 respectively shall be fulfilled automatically. [UN R148 para 4.6.2]

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided no restriction on use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s). [UN R148 para 4.7.1]

The lamp, including the LED modules on PCB and driving circuitry (P-07), shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle. [UN R148 para 4.7.2.3]

Because the lamp is equipped with non-replaceable light sources (or light source modules), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp. [UN R148 para 4.8.1.2]
If not otherwise specified, luminous intensities of each lamp function shall be measured with the light source continuously lit. [UN R148 para 4.8.1.7]

In case measurement results are challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation. [UN R148 para 4.8.1.8.3]
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 6.75 V (6 Volt systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt systems) or 28 V (24 Volt systems). [UN R148 para 4.8.2]

CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control): the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant. [UN R148 para 4.8.2.1]

CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and is equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s)): the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant. [UN R148 para 4.8.2.2]

If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function (rear position, stop, reversing), the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]

If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall not exceed, in any direction where the lamp is visible, the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]

If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples outside the reference axis shall be not less than either: the minimum in the paragraph 5 table of the pertinent function multiplied by the percentage given for each direction in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3; or the intensity value given for each direction in the pertinent light distribution figure of Annex 3. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]

If not otherwise specified, for each lamp function, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2 of UN R148 shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]
For each lamp function, the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 of UN R148 on local variations of luminous intensity shall be observed. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.1]

CONDITIONAL (if an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function is deemed to be a single lamp): the assembly shall comply with the maximum intensity requirements when all lamps together are lit. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.2]

CONDITIONAL (if an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function is deemed to be a single lamp): the assembly shall comply with the minimum intensity requirements when either lamp has failed. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.2]

CONDITIONAL (if the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system 'Y'): the interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements of UN R148 when all its interdependent lamps are operated together. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.3]

CONDITIONAL (if an interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a fixed component and partly on a movable component): the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s). The inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if these lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution at all fixed positions of the movable component(s). [UN R148 para 4.8.3.3]

CONDITIONAL (if a variable intensity control is used, R2/S2): the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.4.1]

CONDITIONAL (if a variable intensity control is used): the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 of UN R148 for the specific lamp. This applies under night-time conditions for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, and under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens) for other systems. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.4.2]
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities of each lamp function shall be carried out according to Annex 8 of UN R148. [UN R148 para 4.8.3.6]

The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function (red for rear position and stop lamps through outer lens P-04; white for reversing lamp through the clear window) shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3 of UN R148, applying the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. [UN R148 para 4.9]

Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3 of UN R148, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted by each lamp function shall be observed. [UN R148 para 4.9]

The rear position lamp function (P-01), which is also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp, shall emit light such that each of the two samples submitted meets the requirements of UN R148 Table 4 (para 5.2.1).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp: the rear position lamp shall be permitted a luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane (UN R148 para 5.2.1 exception to Table 4).
CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady): the rear position lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady) and used as a single lamp: the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady) and the lamp is marked "D": the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.5 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).
CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady): the rear position lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R1 (steady): the rear position lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 5·10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.2.1, Table 4).
CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity): the rear position lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity) and used as a single lamp: the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 4.2·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity) and the lamp is marked "D": the rear position lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.1·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity): the rear position lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.2.1, Table 4).

CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is category R2 (variable intensity): the rear position lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 5·10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.2.1, Table 4).
The rear position lamp (also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp) shall comply with the failure provisions of UN R148 paragraph 4.6 (para 5.2.6).
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp (also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp) shall be red (UN R148 para 5.2.7).
The stop lamp function (P-02) shall emit light such that each of the two samples submitted meets the requirements of UN R148 Table 7 (para 5.5.1).
CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady): the stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady) and used as a single lamp: the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady) and the lamp is marked "D": the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 1.30·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady): the stop lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.5.1, Table 7).

CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S1 (steady): the stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 3·10^-1 cd within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).

CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity) and used as a single lamp: the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 7.30·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).

CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity) and the lamp is marked "D": the stop lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.65·10^2 cd (UN R148 para 5.5.1, Table 7).
CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-I (para 5.5.1, Table 7).

CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 3·10^-1 cd (day) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.5.1, Table 7).

CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is category S2 (variable intensity): the stop lamp shall provide a minimum luminous intensity of 7·10^-2 cd (night) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in UN R148 Table A2-1 (para 5.5.1, Table 7).
The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of UN R148 paragraph 4.6 (para 5.5.6).
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red (UN R148 para 5.5.7).
The reversing lamp function (P-03, category AR) shall emit light such that each of the two samples submitted meets the requirements of UN R148 Table 10 (para 5.8.1).

CONDITIONAL – if the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices: the reversing lamp shall satisfy a photometric value of at least 2.5·10^1 cd at an angle of 30° inwards, with the photometric intensity permitted to be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards (UN R148 para 5.8.1).
The reversing lamp (AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0·10^1 cd (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
The reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 3.00·10^2 cd in or above the h-plane (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
The reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 6.00·10^2 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).
The reversing lamp (AR) shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 8.00·10^3 cd below 5°D (UN R148 para 5.8.1, Table 10).

The reversing lamp (AR) shall provide the standard light distribution according to UN R148 Figure A3-V (para 5.8.1, Table 10). Table 10 sets no geometric visibility intensity requirement for AR (N.A.).
The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of UN R148 paragraph 4.6 (para 5.8.6).
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white (UN R148 para 5.8.7).
Production rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved under UN R148 (para 6.1).
For production lamps, no measured value of the rear position, stop or reversing lamp functions shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148 (para 6.1.3).

For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in UN R148 Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall correspond to Table 12 (para 6.1.3), as follows (required minimum → 20 per cent equivalent / 30 per cent equivalent):
- 7·10^-1 cd → 5·10^-1 cd / 3·10^-1 cd
- 6·10^-1 cd → 4·10^-1 cd / 2·10^-1 cd
- 3·10^-1 cd → 2·10^-1 cd / 1·10^-1 cd
- 7·10^-2 cd → 5·10^-2 cd / 3·10^-2 cd
- 5·10^-2 cd → 3·10^-2 cd / 2·10^-2 cd

[Part 1 of 2, horizontal angles] The rear position lamp function (P-01, class R1 or R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. Where the lamp is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal angles below the H-plane shall be 20° inboard and 80° outboard. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0223)

[Part 2 of 2, vertical angles] The rear position lamp function (P-01, class R1 or R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. The following exceptions apply: 15° above and 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above and 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0223)

[Part 1 of 2, horizontal angles] Where the rear position lamp function (P-01) is deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1/RM2), it shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard and 80° outboard. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0225)

[Part 2 of 2, vertical angles] Where the rear position lamp function (P-01) is deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1/RM2), it shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. The following exceptions apply: 15° above and 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above and 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0225)

[Part 1 of 2, horizontal angles] The stop lamp function (P-02, class S1 or S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. Where the lamp is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum horizontal angles below the H-plane shall be 20° inboard and 45° outboard. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0226)

[Part 2 of 2, vertical angles] The stop lamp function (P-02, class S1 or S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. The following exceptions apply: 15° above and 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5° above and 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm. (Source: UN R148, Annex 2, Table A2-1; parent obligation R148-base-0226)

Unless specified otherwise, each lamp function (rear position lamp P-01, stop lamp P-02, reversing lamp P-03) shall produce, in the various directions of measurement, a luminous intensity of at least the minimum intensities shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV. These minima are expressed as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with H = 0°, V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis. Exception: for the rear position lamp, the rear end-outline marker lamp and the S1/S2 stop lamp intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H-plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 1.1)

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid (Annex 3), the luminous intensity of each lamp function in each direction within a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall be at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding that direction. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 1.2)

For the reversing lamp function (P-03), if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no luminous intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 1.2)

The rear position lamp function (P-01, R1/R2, including its use as a deemed rear end-outline marker lamp) and the stop lamp function (P-02, S1/S2) shall each meet, in the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities shown in Figure A3-I, expressed as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 2.1)

The reversing lamp function (P-03, class AR) shall meet, in the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V. (Source: UN R148, Annex 3, para. 2.5)

From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced lamps shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 4, para. 1.1)

For conformity of production, when the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8 are tested on any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3 of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 5 para. 1.2 as cited)

Mass-produced lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop functions; white for the reversing function) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 4, para. 1.3)

The lamp shall withstand a heat resistance test consisting of one hour of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes, at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C. (Source: UN R148, Annex 6, para. 1)

For the heat resistance test, the lamp equipped with non-replaceable LED light sources shall be tested with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5 of UN R148. If replaceable light sources are used, the light source shall be of the category specified for the lamp and supplied at a voltage giving the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage. (Source: UN R148, Annex 6, para. 1)

In the heat resistance test, the specified average or maximum power shall be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value. For the lamp equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the test conditions of paragraph 5.4.5 or 5.9.5 of UN R148 shall be applied. (Source: UN R148, Annex 6, para. 2)

CONDITIONAL: If any function uses light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity (e.g. rear position lamp class R2 and/or stop lamp class S2), the heat resistance test shall be carried out at a minimum of 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity. (Source: UN R148, Annex 6, para. 2.1)

After the heat resistance test and stabilization at ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp (including the outer lens P-04 and housing P-08) shall be perceptible. (Source: UN R148, Annex 6, para. 3)

In case of doubt after the heat resistance test, the luminous intensity of each lamp function measured according to paragraph 5 shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained on the same lamp before the heat resistance test. (Source: UN R148, Annex 6, para. 3)

The reversing lamp function (P-03), using light source technology other than incandescent only (LED), shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements when measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 1.2.1)

The rear position lamp function (P-01) and the stop lamp function (P-02), using light source technology other than incandescent only (LED), shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements when measured after 1 minute and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 1.2.2)

Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall, in addition to paragraph 1 of Annex 8, comply at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1 of UN R148. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1)
The rear position lamp function (P-01) shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements at reference coordinate HV at 4 seconds after switch ON. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1, Table A8-1)
The stop lamp function (P-02) shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements at reference coordinate HV at 0.2 seconds after switch ON. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1, Table A8-1)

The rear position lamp function (P-01), in its deemed role as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1/RM2), shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements at reference coordinate HV at 4 seconds after switch ON. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1, Table A8-1)
The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements at reference coordinate HV at 0.2 seconds after switch ON. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1, Table A8-1)

Each lamp function using LED technology only shall be deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 of Annex 8 are compliant. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1.2)

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), each lamp function shall comply with the corresponding minimum intensity requirements at all points in time, from the point in time listed in Table A8-1 (4 s for the rear position/end-outline marker lamp; 0.2 s for the stop and reversing lamps) until photometric stability is reached. (Source: UN R148, Annex 8, para. 2.1.5)

[R48 §5.1] The rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector functions) shall be so fitted to the M1 vehicle that, under normal conditions of use (R48 §§2.3.10, 2.3.10.1 and 2.3.10.2) and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of R48.
[R48 §5.1] When the rear combination lamp is fitted to the vehicle, it shall not be possible for the lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.

[R48 §5.3] For each light-signalling function of the rear combination lamp, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

[R48 §5.3] For each light-signalling function of the rear combination lamp (none being a side retro-reflector or side-marker lamp), the reference axis when fitted shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
[R48 §5.3] Any specific instructions laid down by the manufacturer for fitting the rear combination lamp (light-signalling device) shall be complied with when the lamp is installed on the vehicle.

[R48 §5.4] In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the installed rear combination lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in R48 §§2.3.10, 2.3.10.1 and 2.3.10.2, and, where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.

[R48 §5.5.1] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane. This is to be estimated from the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not from the edge of its illuminating surface.

[R48 §5.5.2] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane. This requirement does not apply to the interior structure of the lamp.
[R48 §5.5.3] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.

[R48 §5.5.4] In the absence of specific instructions, the rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This does not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

[R48 §5.5.5] CONDITIONAL – if a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear combination lamp: only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
[R48 §5.5.5] CONDITIONAL – if a logo is incorporated in the rear combination lamp: the logo shall be a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo; all other logos in lamps are prohibited.

[R48 §5.7.1] Where the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another in the rear combination lamp, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and any other applicable requirements shall be fulfilled for each function.

[R48 §5.7.1.1] The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF. Exception: where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions that can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of those other functions shall be fulfilled when those reciprocally incorporated functions and the rear position lamp are switched ON.

[R48 §5.7.2.2] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of a single lamp as defined in R48 §2.4.11.1(b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked 'D' or two independent retro-reflectors: it shall be installed such that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps/retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing these projections, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm.
[R48 §5.7.2.3] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of a single lamp as defined in R48 §2.4.11.1(d) (interdependent lamp system marked 'Y'): it shall fulfil the requirements of R48 §5.7.2.1.

[R48 §5.7.2.3] Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included in the common lamp body (P-08) and/or have the common outer lens (P-04) of the rear combination lamp, they shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system. However, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

[R48 §5.8] The maximum height above the ground of each installed lamp function shall be measured from the highest point, and the minimum height from the lowest point, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis. Where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
[R48 §5.8.1] For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height above the ground of each lamp function shall be measured from the H plane.

[R48 §5.8.3] The width position of each lamp function shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis, that is furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps. Where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

[R48 §5.9] In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

[R48 §5.9.2] Any variation of the photometric characteristics of a lamp function of the rear combination lamp in relation to ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is used to provide another lighting function, shall comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

[R48 §5.10.1] Red light emitted by the rear combination lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle. No account is taken of interior lighting devices or of reversing projections.

[R48 §5.10.4.1] There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red lamp functions of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp) when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (R48 Annex 4).

[R48 §5.10.4.3] In case of doubt, compliance with R48 §§5.10.4.1 and 5.10.4.2 shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front by each red lamp function of the rear combination lamp, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

[R48 §5.11.1] The electrical connections of the rear position lamp function shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if any), the side-marker lamps (if any) and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously. This does not apply: while front and rear position lamps (and side-marker lamps combined or reciprocally incorporated with them) are switched ON as parking lamps; while side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; while daytime running lamps are switched ON; or while the front position lamp function is substituted under R48 §5.12.1.
[R48 §5.11.2] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system: all light sources of the system shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

[R48 §5.13] Where R48 prescribes a closed-circuit tell-tale for a function of the rear combination lamp, that tell-tale may be replaced by an 'operating' tell-tale (permissive provision; no additional lamp-level obligation).

[R48 §5.14.1] The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp shall not be concealed. Only main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps may be concealed when not in use.
[R48 §5.15] The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function of the rear combination lamp shall be as listed in the table of R48 §5.15.
[R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be white.
[R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp function (P-02) shall be red.
[R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp function (P-01) shall be red.
[R48 §5.15, Table 5.15] The colour of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be red.

[R48 §5.16.1] The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and non-triangular rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of R48.

[R48 §5.22] Each lamp function of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing) shall be operable when installed. A lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse. This deeming rule does not apply to the retro-reflector.

[R48 §5.26] CONDITIONAL – if the rear position lamp is of category R2 and/or the stop lamp is of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control: the control shall respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions of R48 §§5.26.1 and 5.26.2 and shall comply with conditions (a) and (b) of R48 §5.26 (see R48-base-0131 and R48-base-0132).

[R48 §5.26(a)] CONDITIONAL – if variable-intensity rear position lamps (R2) and stop lamps (S2) are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated in the rear combination lamp: their luminous intensity shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

[R48 §5.26(b)] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity (R2/S2) is used: throughout the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

[R48 §5.26.1] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity (R2/S2) is used: any increase or decrease of luminous intensity in relation to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light-emitting surface shall remain within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.

[R48 §5.26.2] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity (R2/S2) is used: independent of environmental conditions, a decrease of luminous intensity within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations shall be activated only while the vehicle speed is ≤ 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is ≤ 20 m. A decrease already activated may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is ≤ 50 km/h.

[R48 §5.26.3] CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp is of category S4: it may produce variable luminous intensity based on the conditions of R48 §§5.26.1 and 5.26.2, independently of the other lamps (permissive provision).
[R48 §5.26.4] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity is used: no sharp variation of luminous intensity shall be observed during transitions of the variable-intensity lamp functions.
[R48 §5.26.4] CONDITIONAL – if variable intensity is used: the driver may be enabled to set the variable-intensity lamp functions to static luminous intensities (permissive provision).

[R48 §5.27.1] CONDITIONAL – if the stop lamp (§2.5.4) and/or rear position lamp (§2.5.7) functions were type approved with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode, or at a voltage requested by the applicant: for the M1 vehicle, with the electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the vehicle category, the voltage supplied at the device terminals shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as approved. This does not apply to devices that include an electronic light source control gear, to devices with a variable intensity control as part of the device, or to devices with only light sources approved according to UN R128.

[R48 §5.27.2] CONDITIONAL – in all electric power supply conditions not covered by R48 §5.27.1, with the M1 vehicle electrical system in a representative constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the stop lamp (§2.5.4) and rear position lamp (§2.5.7) functions shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent. This does not apply to devices that include an electronic light source control gear, to devices with a variable intensity control as part of the device, or to devices with only light sources approved according to UN R128.
[R48 §5.27.2] CONDITIONAL – if a means of controlling the maximum voltage at the device terminals is required: it may be located within the body of the rear combination lamp (permissive provision).

[R48 §5.28.1] When installed, there shall be no obstacle inside the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp, observed from infinity. No account is taken of obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.
[R48 §5.28.5] CONDITIONAL – if the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system: the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
[R48 §5.29] The LED modules (P-07) of the rear combination lamp may be non-replaceable only if this is stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval (R148).

[R48 §5.30] Each lamp function of the rear combination lamp installed on the vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulation specified in the relevant subparagraphs of R48 §6 (per product description: R148 for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps; R150 for the non-triangular rear retro-reflector).
[R48 §5.30.1] CONDITIONAL – if the rear combination lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo: the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN R148.

[R48 §5.33] If the rear combination lamp is type approved according to a preceding series of amendments to UN R148 and/or R150, it is deemed equivalent to a device approved to the latest series when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ. It may then be fitted on the vehicle without any update of the device type approval documents and device markings.

[UN R48 para 6.4.1] The M1 motor vehicle on which the rear combination lamp is installed shall be fitted with a reversing lamp (presence mandatory). The reversing lamp function (P-03) of the rear combination lamp is intended to provide this mandatory reversing lamp.
[UN R48 para 6.4.2.1] On the M1 vehicle, one reversing lamp shall be fitted (mandatory); a second reversing lamp is optional. The reversing lamp function (P-03) counts towards this number.

[UN R48 para 6.4.2.3] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

[UN R48 para 6.4.4.2] The reversing lamp function (P-03), as installed on the M1 vehicle, shall be positioned not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground. (The increased maximum of 1,400 mm permitted for categories N2G, N3G, M2G and M3G (off-road) does not apply to M1.)

[UN R48 para 6.4.4.3] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle. (The exception allowing side fitting applies only to the two optional devices of para 6.4.2.2, provided paras 6.4.5.2 and 6.4.6.2 are fulfilled; it does not apply to this rear-mounted lamp.)

[UN R48 para 6.4.5.1] For the reversing lamp function (P-03) installed at the rear, geometric visibility shall be ensured in the vertical direction defined by angle α (para 2.10.7) = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.

[UN R48 para 6.4.5.1] For the reversing lamp function (P-03) installed at the rear, geometric visibility shall be ensured in the horizontal direction defined by angle β = 45° to the right and to the left if there is only one reversing lamp device, and 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two reversing lamp devices.
[UN R48 para 6.4.6.1] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be oriented rearwards.

[UN R48 para 6.4.7.1] The electrical connections of the reversing lamp function (P-03) shall be such that it can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position in which operation of the propulsion system is possible.

[UN R48 para 6.4.7.1] The reversing lamp function (P-03) shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system start/stop device is not in a position allowing operation of the propulsion system.
[UN R48 para 6.4.8] A tell-tale for the reversing lamp function (P-03) is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure shall be provided if required by the component regulation (UN R148).

The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with stop lamp devices of category S1 or S2; the stop lamp function (P-02) of the rear combination lamp provides this mandatory S1 or S2 category device. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.1]
The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with two stop lamp devices of category S1 or S2. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.2]
The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with one stop lamp device of category S3 or S4. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.2]

The stop lamp device (P-02) shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.2]

On the M1 vehicle, the point on the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02), in the direction of the reference axis, that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.1]

The S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02) shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 2,100 mm only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and the optional lamps are not installed. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.2.1]

The horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of the vehicle's S3 or S4 category stop lamp shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamps (P-02). [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.2.2]
In length, the S1 or S2 category stop lamps (P-02) shall be at the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.4.4]

As installed, the S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02) shall provide horizontal geometric visibility of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle. For S1 and S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.5]

As installed, the S1 or S2 category stop lamp (P-02) shall provide vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal. Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°. Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the upward angle may be reduced to 5°. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.5]
The stop lamps (P-02) shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.6]
All stop lamps, including P-02, shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.7.1]

Where the device that starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate, the stop lamps (P-02) are permitted not to function. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.7.2]
A tell-tale for the stop lamps is optional. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.8]
If the component regulation (UN R148) requires it for the stop lamp (P-02), the vehicle shall be fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.7.8]
The M1 vehicle shall be fitted with rear position lamps of category R, R1 or R2; the rear position lamp function (P-01) provides this mandatory device. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.1]
The number of rear position lamps on the M1 vehicle shall be two. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.2]

The rear position lamps (P-01) shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.2]

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp (P-01), in the direction of the reference axis, that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. This condition does not apply to optional rear position lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.4.1]

The rear position lamps (P-01) shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 2,100 mm only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and the optional lamps are not installed. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.4.2]
In length, the rear position lamps (P-01) shall be at the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.4.3]

As installed, the rear position lamp (P-01) shall provide horizontal geometric visibility of 45° inwards and 80° outwards. Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.5.1]

As installed, the rear position lamp (P-01) shall provide vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal. Where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°. Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the upward angle may be reduced to 5°. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.5.1]
The rear position lamps (P-01) shall be oriented rearwards. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.6]

The electrical connections of the rear position lamps (P-01) shall be in accordance with para. 5.11 of UN R48. Exception: if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction indicator, the rear position lamp on the relevant side, or its reciprocally incorporated part, may be switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.7]

The vehicle shall be fitted with a closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps (P-01). This requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.8]
The closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps (P-01) shall be combined with that of the front position lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.8]

If the component regulation (UN R148) requires it for the rear position lamp (P-01), the vehicle shall be fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamps. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.10.8]
The distance between the vehicle's rear fog lamp and each stop lamp, including P-02, shall be greater than 100 mm in all cases. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.11.9]
The M1 motor vehicle shall be fitted with non-triangular rear retro-reflectors; the integral retro-reflector (P-05) provides this mandatory device. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.1]
The number of non-triangular rear retro-reflectors on the M1 vehicle shall be two. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.2]

The non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be type-approved according to the requirements for Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.2]

The point on the illuminating surface of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.4.1]

The non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be mounted not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), and 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.4.2]
In length, the non-triangular rear retro-reflectors (P-05) shall be at the rear of the vehicle. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.4.3]
As installed, the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall provide horizontal geometric visibility of 30° inwards and outwards. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.5]

As installed, the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall provide vertical geometric visibility of 10° above and below the horizontal. Where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to para. 5.8.1), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.5]
The non-triangular rear retro-reflectors (P-05) shall be oriented rearwards. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.6]

The illuminating surface of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (P-05) is permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear, such as P-01 or P-02. [UN R48 9.3.0, para. 6.14.7]

[UN R48 rev. 9.3.0, para. 6.19.7.5; parent obligation R48-base-0614] When the daytime running lamps of the M1 vehicle are switched ON, the vehicle electrical installation shall switch ON the rear position lamp function (P-01) of the rear combination lamp. Exception: the rear position lamps may be switched OFF while the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain OFF, as long as the ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux, measured according to UN R48 Annex 13.

[UN R48 rev. 9.3.0, para. 6.19.7.5; parent obligation R48-base-0615] When the daytime running lamps of the M1 vehicle are switched ON, any other lamp(s) mentioned in UN R48 paragraph 5.11 that are part of this rear combination lamp may also be switched ON. Where such lamps are switched ON with the daytime running lamps, they may be switched OFF while the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain OFF, as long as the ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux, measured according to UN R48 Annex 13.

Per UN R48 (version 9.3.0) para. 6.27.9.1, the stop lamp function (P-02) of the rear combination lamp shall not be used for the answer-back signal. Para. 6.27.9.1 also excludes front fog lamps and rear fog lamps; those functions are not part of this product and are not covered by this requirement.

Each production M1 vehicle approved pursuant to UN R48 and fitted with the rear combination lamp shall be so manufactured as to conform to the approved vehicle type by meeting the requirements set out in UN R48 paragraphs 5 and 6. As identified in the applicability analysis, this covers the installed rear position lamp (para 6.10), stop lamp (para 6.7), reversing lamp (para 6.4), non-triangular rear retro-reflector (para 6.14) and the grouping or reciprocal incorporation of these functions (para 5.7). [Source: UN R48 rev. 9.3.0, para 8.1, p. 82; obligation R48-base-0865; applies to the vehicle installation, so it reaches the lamp only indirectly]

CONDITIONAL (applies only if the rear position lamp and stop lamp functions share or overlap apparent surfaces behind the outer lens, i.e. grouped/reciprocally incorporated configuration per Annex 3 Part 7): Where the non-textured outer lens is excluded and '7b' is the apparent surface according to UN R48 paragraph 2.10.2, function F1 shall not be transparent to function F2. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 3 Part 7; parent R48-base-0866]

For conformity of production, the position in width, height and length of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp as installed on the M1 vehicle (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.1; parent R48-base-0904]

For conformity of production, the angles of geometric visibility of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp as installed (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled. Exception: the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in UN R48 paragraph 5.3 for the mounting of light-signalling devices. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.2.1; parent R48-base-0905]

For conformity of production, the visibility towards the front of red light emitted or reflected by the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, red outer lens and red retro-reflector) shall comply with UN R48 paragraph 5.10. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.2.2; parent R48-base-0906]

For conformity of production, the visibility towards the rear of white light emitted by the rear combination lamp shall comply with UN R48 paragraph 5.10. The reversing lamp is exempt from this restriction only to the extent that paragraph 5.10 itself provides. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.2.2; parent R48-base-0906]

For conformity of production, with every lamp supplied by the vehicle electrical system switched on, the LED-powered rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp, and any associated tell-tales, shall function in accordance with UN R48 paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.4; parent R48-base-0916]

For conformity of production, the presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, category of each lamp function of the rear combination lamp (red rear position lamp, red stop lamp, white reversing lamp and red rear retro-reflector) shall be such that the requirements of UN R48 paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled. [Source: UN R48 Rev 9.3.0, Annex 9 para 1.6; parent R48-base-0918]
The retro-reflector (P-05) shall be marked with the approval number assigned to its approved type, following the requirements of UN R150 paragraph 3.3. [UN R150 para. 3.2.3]

The identification symbol of the retro-reflector (P-05) shall be 'IA' if it is a retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent), or 'IB' if it is a retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight. [UN R150 para. 3.2.5, Table 1]
The approval marking size 'a' for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector (P-05) shall be at least 5 mm. [UN R150 para. 3.2.5, Table 1]

Every retro-reflector (P-05) belonging to the approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for either (a) the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or (b) the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. [UN R150 para. 3.3.1.1]
All markings on the retro-reflective device (P-05) shall be clearly legible. [UN R150 para. 3.3.1.2]
All markings on the retro-reflective device (P-05) shall be indelible. [UN R150 para. 3.3.1.2]
The size of the approval marking on the retro-reflector (P-05) shall be based on the value 'a' defined in UN R150 Table 1 (minimum 5 mm for Class IA/IB). [UN R150 para. 3.3.1.3; see R150-base-0004]

The approval marking of the retro-reflector (P-05) shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval. [UN R150 para. 3.3.2.1]

The approval marking of the retro-reflector (P-05) shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2. [UN R150 para. 3.3.2.2]
The four- to six-digit sequential number of the approval marking of the retro-reflector (P-05) shall be placed close to the approval mark. [UN R150 para. 3.3.2.2]
The approval marking of the retro-reflector (P-05) shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5 (IA or IB). [UN R150 para. 3.3.2.3]

The approval marking of the retro-reflector (P-05) shall include the number of this Regulation (150) followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval. [UN R150 para. 3.3.2.4]

The approval marking defined in UN R150 paragraph 3.3.2 may be replaced on the retro-reflector (P-05) by the Unique Identifier, if available. Where this option is used, the Unique Identifier shall be applied in place of the approval marking. [UN R150 para. 3.3.3.1]
The retro-reflective device (P-05) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant. [UN R150 para. 3.3.4.1]

If an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer, the Class IA/IB retro-reflector (P-05) shall bear the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface. [UN R150 para. 3.3.4.2]
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4, shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device (P-05). [UN R150 para. 3.3.5.1]

Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps of the rear combination lamp (R148 lamp functions and the R150 retro-reflector P-05) have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed. [UN R150 para. 3.3.6.1]

Where a single approval mark is used on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it may be located anywhere on the lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation. [UN R150 para. 3.3.6.1.1; parent R150-base-0022]

Where a single approval mark is used on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be located so that no part of the lamps that transmits light (e.g. outer lens P-04, retro-reflector P-05) can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier. [UN R150 para. 3.3.6.1.2; parent R150-base-0022]

Where a single approval mark is used on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of its components shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations (R148, R150) under which approval has been granted. [UN R150 para. 3.3.6.2]

The retro-reflector (P-05) approved under UN R150 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R150. [UN R150 para. 3.5.1]

The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications', and the Annexes referenced therein, of UN Regulation No. 48 (series of amendments in force at the time of application for type approval) that are pertinent to the rear retro-reflector (P-05) and to vehicle category M1 shall apply to P-05 where their verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible. [UN R150 para. 4]
The retro-reflective device (P-05) shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use. [UN R150 para. 4.1.1]
The retro-reflective device (P-05) shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition. [UN R150 para. 4.1.1]
The components of the retro-reflective device (P-05), or parts thereof, shall not be capable of being easily dismantled. [UN R150 para. 4.1.2]
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be easy to clean. [UN R150 para. 4.1.4]
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not be rough. [UN R150 para. 4.1.4]
Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not prevent easy cleaning. [UN R150 para. 4.1.4]
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector (P-05) when in normal use. [UN R150 para. 4.1.5]

If the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless optical unit P-05 behind the red outer lens P-04 acting as filter), the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use. [UN R150 para. 4.1.6.1]
The retro-reflecting optical unit (P-05) and any filter of the retro-reflector (e.g. P-04 where acting as filter) shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish. [UN R150 para. 4.1.6.2]

When the red retro-reflector (P-05) is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in UN R150 Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected (red) as defined in UN Regulation No. 48. [UN R150 para. 4.2.1.2]
The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5 when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.1, p.11]

The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5 when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.1, p.11]

The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7 that apply to the nature of its materials and construction. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.1, p.11]
The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

At least one hour after the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6, the rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

At least one hour after the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6, the rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall meet the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

The two Class IA/IB retro-reflector (P-05) samples that give the minimum and the maximum RI values after the heat resistance test shall meet the complete photometric requirements of paragraph 5.1.4. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]
The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the water penetration test of Part 2 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

If the water penetration test of Part 2 of Annex 6 is satisfactory, the rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall then be subjected to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants of Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]
CONDITIONAL – if necessary: the rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

CONDITIONAL – if necessary: after the corrosion test, the rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective devices in Part 3 of Annex 4. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]
The rear retro-reflector (P-05), Class IA or IB, shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.1, p.11]

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflectors (P-05) in each group shall have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.2.1, p.12]

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflectors (P-05) in each group shall have an RI that satisfies paragraph 5.1.4. This is verified only at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.3.2.2, p.12]

For photometric measurement of the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05), only the illuminating surface shall be considered. This surface is defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and lies within a circle of 200 mm diameter. The illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm². The surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not reach this area. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.3, p.12]

The RI values of the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05), measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, shall be equal to or greater than the values in Table 3, expressed in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1, p.12]

At an angle of divergence of 20', the red Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall have an RI of at least 3.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, at least 2.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and at least 1.00·10^2 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1 Table 3, p.12]

At an angle of divergence of 1°30', the red Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall have an RI of at least 5·10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, at least 2.8·10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and at least 2.5·10^0 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1 Table 3, p.12]

Within the solid angle that has the centre of reference as its apex and is bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall have no RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.4.4.1, p.12]

When the night-time colour of the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) is tested according to paragraph 4.2.1, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48. The regulation text permits red, amber or white; red applies to this product. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.5.2, p.13]

The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C), assessed by visual inspection for distortion. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
