After the heat test of Part 1 of Annex 6, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the water test (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

After the water test, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the motor fuels test of Part 1 of Annex 7 (5 min), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the oils test of Part 2 of Annex 7 (5 min), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

After the motor fuels and oils tests of Annex 7, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

CONDITIONAL – where the corrosion test is necessary per paragraph 5.1.3.1: the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, 2-hour interval, 24 hours), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

CONDITIONAL – where the rear face test is necessary per paragraph 5.1.3.1: the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall withstand the rear face test (1 min), assessed by visual inspection. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

CONDITIONAL – where the rear face test is performed: after the rear face test, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be subjected to the stability-in-time test of Part 3 of Annex 4. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

After the stability-in-time test of Part 3 of Annex 4, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]
The Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

After the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6, the Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall meet the colorimetry requirements and the photometry requirements, the latter limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°. [UN R150 rev 1.2.1, para. 5.1.7 Table 4, p.14]

From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced units of the rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB, red) shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R150. [UN R150 Annex 2 para. 1.1, p.25]

When the photometric performance of any randomly chosen mass-produced rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB) is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in UN R150. [UN R150 Annex 2 para. 1.2, p.25]
Mass-produced units of the red rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed in UN R150. [UN R150 Annex 2 para. 1.3, p.25]

When the RI of the rear retro-reflector (P-05) is measured for β1 = β2 = 0°, and a mirror effect is produced when the device is turned slightly, the reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°. [UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.1, p.28]

If, for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0°, the RI of the rear retro-reflector (P-05) exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°. [UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 1.4, p.28]

For testing retro-reflection, the rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4, using the CIE angular system. [UN R150 Annex 4 Part 1 para. 3.3, p.30]

The shape of the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB) shall not be easily confused, from an observation distance of 10 metres, with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA and IIIB retro-reflectors. [UN R150 Annex 5 para. 1.1, p.33]

The moulded plastics reflector of the rear retro-reflector (P-05, Class IA or IB, PMMA) shall withstand the heat resistance test: 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1 para. 1, p.42]

After the heat resistance test of UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the rear retro-reflector (P-05), and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 1 para. 3, p.42; acceptance criterion for R150-base-0210]

CONDITIONAL (applies when the water penetration test route is used, i.e. the watertight / Class IA option): The rear retro-reflector (P-05), whether part of a lamp or not, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the water penetration test. The test is: immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface; then repetition after turning the device through 180° (illuminating surface at the bottom, rear face covered by about 20 mm of water); then immediate immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.1, p.42]

CONDITIONAL (applies when the water penetration test route of Annex 6 Part 2 is used, i.e. the watertight / Class IA option): After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the rear retro-reflector (P-05). If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device has not passed the test. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.2, p.42; acceptance criterion for R150-base-0213]

CONDITIONAL (applies when the water penetration test route of Annex 6 Part 2 is used, i.e. the watertight / Class IA option): If visual inspection after the water penetration test does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the RI of the rear retro-reflector (P-05) shall be measured by the method of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 of UN R150, after the device has been lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside. [UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2 para. 1.3.1, p.42]

CONDITIONAL (applies only if the P-05 retro-reflector is approved as Class IB, i.e. combined with a non-watertight lamp, and the manufacturer requests the alternative): the P-05 retro-reflective device shall be subjected to the moisture test and the dust exposure test of R150 Annex 6 Part 3, as an alternative to the water penetration test. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 1; parent R150-base-0222]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the moisture test, the sample device shall be subjected to a solid cone water spray that completely covers the device. The spray shall be directed downward at 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of the rotating test platform. The precipitation rate at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.1.3; parent R150-base-0223]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the moisture test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1 during the water spray. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.2; parent R150-base-0224]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the moisture test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open. Drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.1; parent R150-base-0225]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected, and the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions): during the moisture test, the rear position lamp (P-01), stop lamp (P-02) and reversing lamp (P-03) functions shall be operated at design voltage. The operating cycle shall be 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate) and 55 min OFF. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.3; parent R150-base-0226]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): the water spray of the moisture test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min). [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.4; parent R150-base-0227]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): after the water spray, the rotation and water spray shall be turned off. The device shall then be allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed before evaluation. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.5; parent R150-base-0228]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): on completion of the moisture test drain period, no standing pool of water shall have formed in the interior of the device. No such pool shall be formable by tapping or tilting the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.6; parent R150-base-0229]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): after the moisture test, the exterior of the device shall be dried with a dry cotton cloth. The RI of the device shall then be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 of R150. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.2.6; parent R150-base-0230]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the dust exposure test, the device shall be exposed in a test chamber of max. 2 m3 internal volume. The chamber shall be charged with 3 to 5 kg of test dust consisting of fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.2; parent R150-base-0231]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open. Drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.5; parent R150-base-0232]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): in the dust exposure test, the mounted device shall be placed no closer than 150 mm to a chamber wall; devices longer than 600 mm shall be horizontally centred. The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible for 2 to 15 s at 15 min intervals, over a total duration of 5 hours, and shall be allowed to settle between agitation periods. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.6; parent R150-base-0233]

CONDITIONAL (Class IB, moisture/dust alternative selected): on completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth. The RI shall then be measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of R150. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 3 para 2.3.7; parent R150-base-0234]

The P-05 retro-reflective device shall be designed to retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 1; parent R150-base-0235]

The resistance of the front surface of the P-05 retro-reflective device to tarnishing shall be checked by corrosion resistance testing per ISO 9227:2017. This check is required particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 1; parent R150-base-0236]

The resistance to deterioration of the protection of the rear face of the P-05 retro-reflective device shall be checked by corrosion resistance testing per ISO 9227:2017. This check is required particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 1; parent R150-base-0236]

For the corrosion test, the complete rear combination lamp (since P-05 is combined with lamps) shall be stripped of all removable parts. It shall then be subjected to a saline mist for 50 hours: two exposure periods of 24 hours each, separated by a 2-hour interval during which the sample is allowed to dry. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 2; parent R150-base-0237]

CONDITIONAL (applies if the retro-reflective device has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion): the saline mist for the corrosion test shall be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 3; parent R150-base-0238]

Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall show no signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 4 para 4.1; parent R150-base-0239]

CONDITIONAL (applies if P-05 is a mirror-backed moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB with an accessible rear face): the accessible rear face shall be treated in this sequence: (1) brushed with a hard nylon brush; (2) a cotton cloth soaked in the n-heptane/toluol mixture defined in Annex 7 Part 1 applied to it for one minute; (3) left to dry; (4) brushed again with the same brush. The whole mirror-backed rear face shall then be covered with Indian ink, and the RI measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 6 Part 5 para 3; parent R150-base-0241]

The outer surface of the P-05 retro-reflective device, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol. After about five minutes the surface shall show no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are not objected to. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 7 Part 1 para 1.1; parent R150-base-0247]

Since P-05 is a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB, its outer surface, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes. The RI shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of R150. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 7 Part 2 para 1.1; parent R150-base-0251]

In the R150 approval mark of the P-05 retro-reflective device, the approval number shall be placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E"; it may be in any position in relation to that circle. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 10; parent R150-base-0284]

In the R150 approval mark of the P-05 retro-reflective device, the digits constituting the approval number shall face the same way as the letter "E". [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 10; parent R150-base-0285]

In the R150 approval mark of the P-05 retro-reflective device, the group of symbols indicating the class (IA or IB) shall be diametrically opposite the approval number. [Source: UN R150 v1.2.1, Annex 10; parent R150-base-0286]

Each rear lamp ESA sample (LED modules on PCB, P-07, within the lamp assembly) submitted for UN R10 approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark. [UN R10 para 3.2.6]
Each rear lamp ESA sample submitted for UN R10 approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with its type designation. [UN R10 para 3.2.6]

Where the rear lamp ESA is (part of) a light source, it shall either hold an approval according to UN Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128, or be shown by a Technical Service test report not to be mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to UN Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128. Otherwise UN R10 approval shall not be granted. [UN R10 para 3.2.10]

Where the vehicle is approved by testing of individual ESAs, the rear lamp ESA, as a relevant ESA (para 3.1.3), shall be approved in accordance with UN R10. It shall be installed in accordance with any conditions attached to its approval. [UN R10 para 4.1.1.2]

An approval mark as described in UN R10 para 5.3 shall be affixed to every rear lamp ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10. No marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles that are approved as units. [UN R10 para 5.2.2]
The UN R10 approval mark on the rear lamp ESA shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval. [UN R10 para 5.3.1]

The UN R10 approval mark on the rear lamp ESA shall comprise, to the right of the circle, the number of UN Regulation No. 10 followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number. [UN R10 para 5.3.2]
The UN R10 approval marking on the rear lamp ESA need not be visible when the lamp is installed in the vehicle. This is a permissive provision. [UN R10 para 5.5]

The rear lamp ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted so as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10. This covers configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid. [UN R10 para 6.1.1]
The rear lamp ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions, conducted emissions, immunity to radiated disturbances and immunity to conducted disturbances. [UN R10 para 6.1.1.2]
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in UN R10 Annex 7. [UN R10 para 6.5.1]

The broadband radiated emission of the rear lamp ESA, measured per UN R10 Annex 7, shall not exceed the following limits (as shown in Appendix 6). In the 30 to 75 MHz band: 62 to 52 dBµV/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz. In the 75 to 400 MHz band: 52 to 63 dBµV/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz. [UN R10 para 6.5.2.1]
The broadband radiated emission of the rear lamp ESA, measured per UN R10 Annex 7, shall not exceed a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band. [UN R10 para 6.5.2.1]
On the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits of UN R10 para 6.5.2.1. [UN R10 para 6.5.2.2]

CONDITIONAL: applies if the rear lamp ESA includes an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz (otherwise para 6.10.1 deems compliance). The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in UN R10 Annex 8. [UN R10 para 6.6.1; see 6.10.1]

CONDITIONAL: applies if the ESA includes an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz. The narrowband radiated emission of the rear lamp ESA, measured per UN R10 Annex 8, shall not exceed the following limits (as shown in Appendix 7). In the 30 to 75 MHz band: 52 to 42 dBµV/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz. In the 75 to 400 MHz band: 42 to 53 dBµV/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz. [UN R10 para 6.6.2.1; see 6.10.1]

CONDITIONAL: applies if the ESA includes an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz. The narrowband radiated emission of the rear lamp ESA, measured per UN R10 Annex 8, shall not exceed a constant 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band. [UN R10 para 6.6.2.1; see 6.10.1]

CONDITIONAL: applies if the ESA includes an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz. On the rear lamp ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits of UN R10 para 6.6.2.1. [UN R10 para 6.6.2.2; see 6.10.1]

CONDITIONAL: applies unless the rear lamp ESA is not switched, contains no switches or does not include inductive load (para 6.10.5). The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the rear lamp ESA representative of its type on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in UN R10 Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 1. [UN R10 para 6.7.1]

CONDITIONAL: applies unless the para 6.10.5 exemption is met. The positive transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the rear lamp ESA on its supply lines shall not exceed +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems, or +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems. [UN R10 para 6.7.1, Table 1]

CONDITIONAL: applies unless the para 6.10.5 exemption is met. The negative transient conducted emission pulse amplitude of the rear lamp ESA on its supply lines shall not exceed -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems, or -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems. [UN R10 para 6.7.1, Table 1]

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type shall be tested by method(s) chosen from those described in UN R10 Annex 9. The test severity shall be per Table 2a over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band, and the minimum test level shall be per Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band. [UN R10 para 6.8.1]

Over more than 90 per cent of the frequency band, the rear lamp ESA radiated immunity test level shall be as follows, depending on the Annex 9 method used [UN R10 para 6.8.2.1, Table 2a]: stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).

Over the whole frequency band, the rear lamp ESA radiated immunity minimum test level shall be as follows, depending on the Annex 9 method used [UN R10 para 6.8.2.1, Table 2b]: stripline 50 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).

During the immunity tests performed in accordance with UN R10 Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the rear lamp ESA's immunity related functions, namely the stop lamp (P-02) and rear position lamp (P-01) functions. [UN R10 para 6.8.2.2]

The immunity of the rear lamp ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested as described in UN R10 Annex 10, at the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b. The starting profile shall be tested per ISO 16750-2, and pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b per ISO 7637-2. [UN R10 para 6.9.1]
The rear lamp ESA starting profile test shall be evaluated according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1. [UN R10 para 6.9.1]
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the rear lamp ESA immunity test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b. [UN R10 para 6.9.1]

This requirement applies where the rear lamp ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor; the starting profile is not applicable otherwise. The ESA shall then withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems), 10 pulses, achieving: functional status B for ESAs related to immunity related functions that shall be operational during engine start phases; C for other ESAs related to immunity related functions; and D for ESAs not related to immunity related functions. [UN R10 para 6.9.1, Table 3a]

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses, achieving FPSC III, whether or not related to immunity related functions. [UN R10 para 6.9.1, Table 3b]

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses. It shall achieve FPSC I as an ESA related to immunity related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp); FPSC III applies only to ESAs not related to immunity related functions. [UN R10 para 6.9.1, Table 3b]

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses. It shall achieve FPSC II as an ESA related to immunity related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp); FPSC III applies only to ESAs not related to immunity related functions. [UN R10 para 6.9.1, Table 3b]

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h. It shall achieve FPSC I as an ESA related to immunity related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp); FPSC III applies only to ESAs not related to immunity related functions. [UN R10 para 6.9.1, Table 3b]

The rear lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h. It shall achieve FPSC I as an ESA related to immunity related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp); FPSC III applies only to ESAs not related to immunity related functions. [UN R10 para 6.9.1, Table 3b]

CONDITIONAL: where the rear lamp ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with UN R10 para 6.6.2 and Annex 8 (narrowband emission). [UN R10 para 6.10.1; relates to R10-base-0046 to R10-base-0049]

CONDITIONAL: where the rear lamp ESA is not switched, contains no switches or does not include inductive load, it need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with UN R10 para 6.7. [UN R10 para 6.10.5; relates to R10-base-0050 to R10-base-0052]

The rear combination lamp approved under UN R10 as an ESA (component or STU; LED modules on PCB P-07 with associated wiring/connector) shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of UN R10 paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.1, p.25; obligation R10-base-0191]

For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp ESA taken from the series, the measured broadband and narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in UN R10 paragraphs 6.5.2.1 and 6.6.2.1 and, if applicable, 7.10.2.1 for ESAs. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.1, p.26; obligation R10-base-0192. The vehicle limits in paras 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.3.2.1, 6.3.2.2, 7.2.2.1 and 7.2.2.2 cited in the same paragraph apply to vehicles, not to this ESA.]

For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp ESA taken from the series, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user, when in the state defined in UN R10 Annex 6, paragraph 4, and subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in UN R10 paragraph 6.8.2.1 and, if applicable, 7.18.2.1 for ESAs. This applies in particular to the immunity related functions: stop lamp (P-02) and rear position lamp (P-01). [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.2, p.26; obligation R10-base-0193]

For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp approved as a component or STU and taken from the series, the lamp shall show no degradation of performance of 'immunity related functions' (stop lamp P-02 and rear position lamp P-01) up to the conducted disturbance levels given in UN R10 paragraph 6.9.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.3, p.26; obligation R10-base-0194]

For conformity of production of the rear combination lamp approved as a component or STU and taken from the series, the conducted transient emission of the lamp shall not exceed the levels given in UN R10 paragraph 6.7.1 and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, para 9.3.3, p.26; obligation R10-base-0195]

The rear combination lamp, as an ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry, P-07), shall not exceed a broadband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 30 MHz to 75 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.5.2.1, Appendix 6; parent obligation R10-base-0206]

The rear combination lamp, as an ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry, P-07), shall not exceed a broadband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 75 MHz to 400 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.5.2.1, Appendix 6; parent obligation R10-base-0206]

The rear combination lamp, as an ESA (LED modules on PCB with driving circuitry, P-07), shall not exceed a broadband radiated electromagnetic interference level of 63 dBµV/m (120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 400 MHz to 1,000 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.5.2.1, Appendix 6; parent obligation R10-base-0207]

Where the LED drive electronics of the rear combination lamp (P-07) are not deemed to comply under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10 (e.g. an active electronic driver with an oscillator, switch-mode/PWM or microcontroller), the lamp as an ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 30 MHz to 75 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.6.2.1, Appendix 7; parent obligation R10-base-0208]

Where the LED drive electronics of the rear combination lamp (P-07) are not deemed to comply under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10, the lamp as an ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated electromagnetic interference level of E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m (F in MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 75 MHz to 400 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.6.2.1, Appendix 7; parent obligation R10-base-0208]

Where the LED drive electronics of the rear combination lamp (P-07) are not deemed to comply under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10, the lamp as an ESA shall not exceed a narrowband radiated electromagnetic interference level of 53 dBµV/m (120 kHz bandwidth) in the frequency range 400 MHz to 1,000 MHz. [UN R10 rev. 7.2.0, para 6.6.2.1, Appendix 7; parent obligation R10-base-0209]

When installed on the M1 vehicle and subjected to the UN R10 vehicle immunity test in 50 km/h mode with dipped beams ON (manual mode), the rear lamp's rear light (rear position lamp function, P-01) shall not go OFF. Going OFF constitutes failure of the immunity test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, Annex 6 para 2.1.1.1, Table '50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions', p.72; obligation R10-base-0244]

source.paragraph: Annex 6 2.1.1.1. Table 50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions

requirements.text: When installed on the M1 vehicle and subjected to the UN R10 vehicle immunity test in 50 km/h mode with the brake pedal not depressed, the rear lamp's stop lamp function (P-02) shall not activate unexpectedly. Unexpected activation of the stop lights constitutes failure of the immunity test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, Annex 6 para 2.1.1.1, Table '50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions', p.72; obligation R10-base-0257]

source.paragraph: Annex 6 2.1.1.1. Table 50 km/h mode vehicle test conditions

requirements.text: When installed on the M1 vehicle and subjected to the UN R10 vehicle immunity test in brake mode, the rear lamp's stop lamp function (P-02) shall not be inactivated at any time during the mode. Brake mode means: the vehicle is in a state allowing the braking system to operate normally, the parking brake is released, vehicle speed is 0 km/h, and the brake pedal is depressed to activate the brake function and stop lights without any dynamic cycle. Inactivation of the stop lights during the mode constitutes failure of the immunity test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0, Annex 6 para 2.1.1.1, Table 'Brake mode vehicle test conditions', p.72; obligation R10-base-0259]

source.paragraph: Annex 6 2.1.1.1. Table Brake mode vehicle test conditions

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA (P-07 LED modules on PCB with drive circuitry and wiring/connector) shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in UN R10 Annex 7. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 1.2; parent R10-base-0292]

During the UN R10 Annex 7 broadband emission test, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 2.1; parent R10-base-0293]

Because the rear lamp ESA is not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', its broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0298]

The rear lamp ESA shall comply with the ESA broadband emission limits of UN R10 para 6.5 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS). [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 4.1; parent R10-base-0301]

The ESA broadband emission limits of UN R10 para 6.5 shall be treated as quasi-peak detector limits. Measurements of the rear lamp ESA may use quasi-peak or peak detectors; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 7 para 4.2; parent R10-base-0302]

CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required for the rear lamp ESA, i.e. the selected LED drive electronics are not deemed compliant under the exceptions of UN R10 para 6.10 (open option: passive vs active driver). Where it applies, the narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in UN R10 Annex 8. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 1.2; parent R10-base-0303]

CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the UN R10 Annex 8 narrowband emission test. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 2; parent R10-base-0304]

CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the narrowband emission test of the rear lamp ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0305]

CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the rear lamp ESA shall comply with the ESA narrowband emission limits of UN R10 para 6.6 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 4.1; parent R10-base-0306]

CONDITIONAL – applies only if narrowband emission testing is required (depends on the LED drive electronics option and the para 6.10 exceptions). Where it applies, the narrowband emission measurements of the rear lamp ESA shall be performed with an average detector. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 8 para 4.2; parent R10-base-0307]

The rear lamp ESA, which is not in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', shall demonstrate compliance with the ESA immunity requirements using any combination of the following methods, at the manufacturer's discretion: absorber chamber (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline (ISO 11452-5) and reverberation chamber (ISO 11452-11). The chosen combination shall cover the full frequency range specified in UN R10 Annex 9 para 3.1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 1.2.1; parent R10-base-0308]

The immunity test conditions for the rear lamp ESA, including frequency range and general test conditions, shall be according to ISO 11452-1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 2.1; parent R10-base-0310]
During the immunity test, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 2.2; parent R10-base-0311]

Immunity measurements of the rear lamp ESA shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time chosen according to ISO 11452-1. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0317]

In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal modulation for the rear lamp ESA shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0318]

In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal modulation for the rear lamp ESA shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0319]

In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal modulation for the rear lamp ESA shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between the Technical Service and the ESA manufacturer. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 3.1; parent R10-base-0320]

Where the absorber chamber method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-2, using the substitution method to establish the test field conditions and with vertical polarization. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.1.2; parent R10-base-0321]

Where the TEM cell method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell, depending on the ESA to be tested. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.2.2; parent R10-base-0324]

Where the bench bulk current injection method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, using either the substitution method with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA or the closed loop method with the injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.3.2; parent R10-base-0325]

As an alternative to the bench BCI test, the rear lamp ESA may be tested for bulk current injection immunity while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4. In that case the substitution method shall be used with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.3.2; parent R10-base-0326]
Where the stripline method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.4.2; parent R10-base-0328]

Where the reverberation chamber method is used for the rear lamp ESA, the immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11, using a test setup with ground plane unless otherwise specified. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 9 para 4.5.2; parent R10-base-0329]

(Part 1 of 2: immunity) The rear lamp ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, as tested according to UN R10 Annex 10. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 1; parent R10-base-0330]

(Part 2 of 2: emission) Conducted transients from the rear lamp ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited, as tested according to UN R10 Annex 10. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 1; parent R10-base-0330]

Test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0331]

Test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0332]

Test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0333]

Test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0334]

Test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0335]

The starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of the rear lamp ESA and to any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. Exception: ESAs reserved exclusively for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor are not subject to the starting profile. The rear lamp is intended for M1 vehicles generally and is not so reserved. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 2; parent R10-base-0336]

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the rear lamp ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2, on the supply lines and on any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. [Source: UN R10 v7.2.0 Annex 10 para 3; parent R10-base-0337]

When installed on an M1 vehicle, the exposed external surface of the rear combination lamp (outer lens P-04 and any exposed housing, seal or retro-reflector portions) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision. (Source: UN R26 para 5.2; parent R26-base-0015)

When installed on an M1 vehicle, the exposed external surface of the rear combination lamp shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists. (Source: UN R26 para 5.3; parent R26-base-0016)

Condition: applies if any part of the installed lamp's external surface protrudes by 5 mm or more. Requirement: no such protruding part of the lamp's external surface (lens, exposed housing edges or other exposed parts) shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, unless the material-hardness provision of para 5.5 applies. (Source: UN R26 para 5.4, first clause; parent R26-base-0017)

Condition: applies if any part of the installed lamp's external surface protrudes by at least 1.5 mm but less than 5 mm. Requirement: the outward-facing angles of such parts shall be blunted. These parts are exempt from the 2.5 mm minimum radius requirement. (Source: UN R26 para 5.4, exception clause; parent R26-base-0017)

Condition: applies to parts of the installed lamp's external surface that protrude less than 1.5 mm. Requirement: such parts are exempt from both the 2.5 mm minimum radius requirement and the requirement to blunt outward-facing angles. They remain subject to paras 5.2 and 5.3. (Source: UN R26 para 5.4, 'save where' clause; parent R26-base-0017)

Condition: applies only if a protruding part of the installed lamp's external surface (e.g. an exposed TPE/silicone seal P-09) has a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm and relies on the soft-material provision. Requirement: that part shall be made of a material with a hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A. (Source: UN R26 para 5.5; parent R26-base-0018)

Condition: applies wherever the para 5.5 soft-material provision is invoked for a lamp part. Requirement: the hardness of that part shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle. Where a Shore A measurement is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation. (Source: UN R26 para 5.5; parent R26-base-0018)

The installed lamp's external surface shall meet the provisions of UN R26 paras 5.1 to 5.5 in addition to any applicable particular specifications of para 6, except where those particular specifications expressly provide otherwise. (Source: UN R26 para 5.6; parent R26-base-0019)

The rear combination lamp, as supplied for installation on approved M1 vehicles, shall be manufactured so that the installed lamp's external surface continues to meet the requirements of UN R26 paras 5 and 6 as approved for the vehicle type (conformity of production). (Source: UN R26 para 8.1; parent R26-base-0079)

Where the rear combination lamp is mounted on a convex external surface of the M1 vehicle, the dimension of the projection of the lamp shall be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the lamp in its installed condition (UN R26 v4.0.0, Annex 3 para 2.1; the regulation permits either method).

Where the rear combination lamp is mounted on a surface other than convex and the dimension of its projection cannot be determined by simple measurement, the dimension of the projection shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over, and is in constant contact with, the lamp (UN R26 v4.0.0, Annex 3 para 2.2, Figure 3).
